edits.name: School lines first in the weekday morning mail text

The model picks out the school mail, with no sender list, and passes on no links; length and layout are tuned on the first two weeks of real mail. edits.example: Trigger: the weekday 07:00 mail text to Tony. It opens: 'School: picture day is Thursday 15 October, order form due Wednesday 14 October; PTA meeting moved to Tuesday 20 October at 7 pm.' The other mail lines follow in the same text.
edits.how: No separate job, no sender list, no check on the search and no stored last-run marker. The school lines are one instruction in the message of the weekday 07:00 job on the owner's mail reader (G015). The short jobs script (G003) creates that job with the owner's handle read from the family file, a time limit and a tool list that holds only Gmail read tools. The instruction: from the last day's mail (three days on a Monday), list first what comes from school, teachers, teams and activities, with each date spelled out and the sender named, and no links. Once the Gmail connection works, read the first two weeks of digests to see which school systems actually send mail; only then change a platform's own digest setting, and only for one that shows up. A hint line of known sender names may be added to the job message if those weeks show misses.

No driver line, no packing line, no household-store read and no dates taken from mail: what a parent wants in the text goes on the calendar. edits.name: Dates from a flyer become reminders after a yes
edits.description: After reading a flyer, slip or schedule, or on a typed request, Happy lists the dates it found, each spelled out in full, and offers to set a reminder for each; nothing is set until the parent says yes. This works once F007 passes its first test and, as things stand, for Tony only: when Jordan sends a flyer Happy lists the dates and sets nothing (Q9). Calendar events are added by a parent on the phone; Happy does not write to the calendar.
edits.example: Tony sends a photo of a season schedule. Happy replies with the eight dates it read, each spelled out in full, flags one that has no start time, and asks whether to set a reminder the evening before each. Nothing is set until he answers; he adds the events to the calendar himself on the phone.
edits.how: A standing rule on the parent's own agent, on top of reminders (F007) and, for a photo or PDF, attachment reading (F002): list every date spelled out in full, set nothing until the parent says yes, then set one reminder per confirmed date. It is a plain conversational proposal, not `ask_user`. Typed requests need only F007. Not built: the calendar write server, its write token and approval step, the calendar-file plugin, the `llm-task` call and any stored rows. House-rules plugin: this card adds no rule of its own; the reminders it sets pass the reminder rule added with F007 (add only, to the asker, no web address, an empty tool list). One eval case before go-live: a planted flyer that asks for a reminder to someone else, or for one without a yes, must create no reminder.
depends_on: F007 reminders live first (wave C); waits on Q6, and on F007's first test that a reminder can be created from an iMessage turn at all
F002 photo and PDF reading (wave B; waits on Q8 part 2), only for dates taken from a photo or PDF
waits on Q9: whether reminders stay Tony's only, which decides what Jordan gets when she sends a flyer
caveats: Dates read from a photo can be wrong (a missing year, two schedules on one sheet, a blurry corner), so every proposal spells each date out in full and nothing is set until the parent says yes.
The yes before a reminder is a prompt rule. What code enforces is the reminder rule that comes with F007: a reminder can only be added, only to the asker, with no web address and no tools.
Happy puts nothing on the calendar. Until a parent adds the events on the phone, they are not in calendar answers (F009) or the evening text (F014).
Reminders are Tony's only as things stand (he said 'no need' to add Jordan to the command list), so a flyer from Jordan gets the list of dates and no reminders unless Q9 is answered the other way.

The phone and Google's assistant already cover part of this: a recent iPhone can offer to add one event from a poster, and Google's Gemini app can create calendar events from details pasted into its chat. Happy's part is a sheet with many dates, or a PDF, handled in the thread the parents already use, with every date spelled out first and a text the evening before.

If a parent later asks Happy for calendar entries, the first step is a five-minute hand test (one calendar file sent from Messages on the Mac and tapped on each phone), not a build. A calendar write, if ever built, needs an approval enforced in code, as the roadmap requires.
edits.safety: Flyer text is outside content read by the parent's own agent, so nothing is set without a yes. A reminder is a way to send later: the reminder rule in the house-rules plugin (added with F007) refuses any target but the asker, any web address and any job that carries tools, and blocks when its own code fails. Nothing is written to a calendar.
unverified: Date extraction accuracy on real flyers (missing years, two schedules on one sheet, blurry photos) has not been measured.
That a reminder can be created from an iMessage turn at all (F007's first test) has not been tried, for Tony either.
Which iPhones the parents carry: the phone-side claim in the caveats rests on press guides, not on Apple's own page.

edits.name: Day-out and trip planner: options with the weather and links
edits.description: 'Plan Saturday for us, rain likely' returns two options, each with the forecast for home, links, opening hours where a page that could be read shows them, and an admission price only when a page that was read showed one. A weekend or longer plan comes back the same way, as a text, with hotels and transport as links, not prices. The parents book; Happy books and pays for nothing.
edits.example: Tony texts: 'Plan Saturday for us, rain likely.' Happy sends two options, one indoors and one outdoors with a rain fallback, each with Saturday's forecast, a link with the time the page was read, opening hours where the venue's page showed them, and the admission price where it showed one.
edits.how: A short planning rule on each parent's agent and on wave B's research helper (F019), plus one hand-off with a time limit. The helper searches and reads venue pages; the forecast for home comes from the existing `home_weather` tool. The answer gives two options with the weather, links and their fetch times, opening hours where a page that could be read shows them, a price only from a page that was read, and nothing booked. The task handed to the helper carries only a place, a distance and dates; the dates come from the parent's request, so no calendar read is needed. Not built: the place lookup with its Google Cloud project, key and wrapper, the Friday text, and the paperwork line for trips abroad. Two eval cases before go-live: a price must come from a fetched page, and a planted page cannot add a booking step.

Prices are best effort. Plain page reads fail on many booking, hotel and transport sites, so those come as links, and an admission price appears only when a page that could be read showed it.

There is no place lookup, so opening hours come only from venue pages that could be read, with no ratings and no drive time; for 'is it open now?' the maps app on the phone is quicker. A place lookup is a later add-on: the roadmap names Google's hosted Maps server, it needs billing switched on, and that has not been put to Tony.
What reaches the research helper (a place, a distance and dates) is an instruction to the parent's agent, not an enforced limit. Whether ages may go too is not confirmed (Q13).
A general assistant such as Gemini already drafts an itinerary from a typed prompt. What this small version adds is the forecast for home in the same answer and arrival in the iMessage thread.
In wave C it gives way after the evening text if the plan is over its ceiling; it may be built at the end of wave B instead if nothing was carried into wave B from wave A.
edits.safety: The research helper holds no family data and has no payment or booking tool; it is given only a place, a distance and dates (a prompt rule on the parent's agent, not an enforced limit). Web pages are outside content: an eval case checks that a planted page cannot add a booking step. Answers go only to the asking parent.
